source.title: Representational Simplicity and Circuit Size Dissociate in a Threshold-Dependent Way: A Controlled Test via Adversarial Training

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates IOI circuit recovery and faithfulness using edge attribution patching, a different method from the original circuit analysis, and reports how circuit size changes with the faithfulness target.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports SAE reconstruction and feature-attribution results, GT results, and IOI qualification accuracies. SAE measures are representational rather than causal-circuit results; GT is explicitly not competence-matched; IOI accuracies serve as qualification checks. These are not rows for the listed circuit claims.
record.test_reason: The study uses the IOI task and EAP-IG edge recovery as a tool to compare circuit size between standard and adversarially trained GPT-2 Small. It never identifies the 26 heads or 7 classes, never checks name-mover backup takeover, and never compares recovered circuits with the original. Its numbers are edge counts and AUCs of its own recovered subgraphs, so they do not bear on whether any version holds.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. Add the representational finding: the robust model is more SAE-decomposable and has fewer active attribution features, though not more concentrated ones. The authors call circuit size regime-dependent, with robust needing fewer edges at 90-95%, a causal result shown only on the primary pair.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses EAP-IG edge attribution and edge-native faithfulness on a raw computational graph, rather than reproducing the original manual circuit identification and its head-class role tests. It also evaluates continually trained standard and adversarial GPT-2 Small models.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported edge count depends on faithfulness target: standard leads at 70%, the models tie at 80–85%, and robust requires fewer edges at 90–95%. EAP-GP and EAP-IG also yield sharply different IOI AUC outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: In the primary pair, which model needs fewer edges flips with the target. Standard needs fewer at 70% (512 vs 1,000) and ties at 80-85%. Robust needs fewer at 90% (1,000 vs 4,000) and 95% (2,000 vs 16,000).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adversarial continual training changes the size of EAP-IG IOI circuits in a faithfulness-threshold-dependent way.

fits_no_version.finding: The 85% edge count stays at 1,000 across the seven-model sweep and the FineWeb pair, except e050-a02 at 2,000.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The 85%-faithfulness IOI circuit size is insensitive to adversarial strength.

fits_no_version.finding: A pilot EAP-GP implementation gives negative IOI AUC (-0.97 and -0.70) against EAP-IG's 0.87 and 0.60.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Circuit-discovery method quality on IOI varies by method, measured as faithfulness AUC.

record.problems: Circuit recovery uses a 200-prompt IOI subsample. The high-faithfulness comparison is reported only for the primary pair; the sweep and FineWeb pair have only 85% crossings. The study uses one base architecture and one adversarial-training regime. Its EAP-GP implementation had no public reference implementation and used a stated shared-gradient-path approximation.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for GT circuit results: the paper says GT is not competence-matched and does not use that curve as evidence for its main IOI comparison. SAE reconstruction, SAE attribution, and qualification accuracy results were also omitted because they do not measure the listed causal-circuit claims.

untested.parts: All of it: no head-level circuit, classes, or the original faithfulness, completeness and minimality tests.
All of it: no ablation of name-mover heads and no identification of takeover heads.
All of it: no head classes or roles in continually trained models, other sizes, or other tasks.
All of it: no overlap between recovered circuits and the original circuit.
All of it: the original circuit's faithfulness and completeness are not evaluated under varied ablations, metrics or prompts.
All of it: ABBA and BABA are pooled, with no template or name-count variation.

record.verdict_notes: The study treats IOI only as a competence-matched benchmark for comparing circuit size. The reader's V1, V2, V4 and V5 links conflate edge-count faithfulness of the study's own EAP-IG subgraphs with claims about the Wang et al. circuit. I removed all verdicts for that reason.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not identify or test the original 26 attention heads, their seven classes, or their stated head-specific roles. Its edge-level faithfulness analysis is not a direct test of the original circuit's completeness or minimality criteria.
Conditional co-ablation tests backup components generally; the study does not specifically ablate the original main name-mover heads or establish that particular heads take over their role.
No cross-model-size, architecture, or training-checkpoint test of the same head classes and roles, and no test of their reuse on other tasks.
The study compares EAP-IG and EAP-GP circuit-recovery outcomes, but does not compare recovered circuit overlap or test alternative ablation types and metrics.

The study varies faithfulness threshold and circuit-recovery method, but does not systematically vary ablation type or prompt distribution; its main circuit-size comparison uses one 200-prompt IOI sample.
IOI circuits are recovered on a combined ABBA/BABA prompt sample, without separate results by order or template, and the study does not test more names or compare components across prompt variants.
